Dylan / Marissa — looked over the counter and ran quick numbers with comp models. My read: candidate is mission-critical and replacement timeline is 4+ months, so there is a reasonable business case for exception, but we should minimize one-time cash exposure. Proposed exception structure (recommended):

1) Sign-on: $45,000 total structured as $30,000 payable at start + $15,000 payable after 12 months (to preserve retention)
2) Equity: approve a 0.08% refresh grant (4-year schedule, standard 1y cliff + monthly thereafter). Convert percent to grant units in the offer letter (approx ~11,500 RSUs at expected strike/value; recruiting to compute final units).
3) Make-whole: we should not fully gross-up for taxes. Offer a capped reimbursement: up to $18,000 with receipts, payable at start. This avoids a full make-whole while acknowledging forfeiture exposure.

Cost sensitivity: net-first-year cash outlay = $48k (30k + up to 18k make-whole if claimed) + $15k deferred = $63k potential, with equity dilution cost equivalent to ~0.08% (cap table admin to sign off).

Approval path: Comp & People sign-off (Director level: Karthik) + VP People or CFO for anything above $50k immediate cash or >0.05% refresh. Since our immediate cash proposed is $30k start (under $50k) and equity is 0.08% (>0.05%), this requires VP approval on equity. Please let me know if you want me to route to Laura or to give you a one-off to present. I can prepare the short memo (1 page) with the cost table and candidate leak risk.
